# Prediction Markets Daily
> **Two states won the right to regulate Kalshi sports contracts as gambling.**

**What You Need to Know:** A federal appeals court has held that Kalshi's sports contracts are not financial swaps, and that Ohio and Tennessee may regulate them under state gambling laws. Kalshi has also suspended three congressional candidates who bet on their own races, while Missouri's attorney general ordered six prediction markets to stop sports bets. Morgan Stanley is now a named partner of the NEXTPredict summit, and JPMorgan has cut Polymarket's banking ties over regulatory concerns.

### Top Story
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit has ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are not financial swaps, Law360 reports. That appeals ruling lets Ohio and Tennessee regulate Kalshi's sports event contracts, Courthouse News, Benzinga, and related reports dated September 26, 2026, all describe. Benzinga frames the result as Kalshi losing a legal battle in which the court said those two states can regulate the contracts under gambling laws. Unchained and a BigGo finance report likewise call it a setback that leaves the states able to police the sports contracts. This is an appeals-court ruling, not a new CFTC rule and not a filing. Source: [law360.com](https://www.law360.com/amp/articles/2530376)

### The Ecosystem
**Kalshi suspends three congressional candidates for betting on their own races: ABC News**
Kalshi has suspended three congressional candidates for betting on their own races, ABC News reports. Source: [abcnews.com](https://abcnews.com/US/prediction-market-kalshi-suspends-3-congressional-candidates-betting/story?id)

**Missouri attorney general orders six prediction markets to end sports bets: The Black Chronicle**
Missouri's attorney general has ordered six prediction markets to end sports bets, The Black Chronicle reports. Source: [blackchronicle.com](https://blackchronicle.com/midwest/missouri/attorney-general-orders-six-prediction-markets-to-end-sports-bets/)

**Morgan Stanley joins NEXTPredict as a named institutional partner: Yahoo Finance**
Morgan Stanley has partnered with prediction-market platform NEXTPredict as a publicly named institutional collaborator, Yahoo Finance reports. The bank will act as a strategic partner at the upcoming NEXTPredict summit and lead discussions on institutional adoption of prediction markets. Yahoo Finance says this is the first time a major Wall Street bank has formally aligned with a prediction-market initiative focused on this emerging asset class. Source: [sg.finance.yahoo.com](https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/morgan-stanley-ms-joins-prediction-100851041.html)

**JPMorgan cut Polymarket banking ties over regulatory concerns: The Fintech Times**
JPMorgan cut Polymarket's banking ties over regulatory concerns, The Fintech Times reports. Source: [thefintechtimes.com](https://thefintechtimes.com/jpmorgan-cut-polymarket-banking-ties-over-regulatory-concerns/)

**Experts and superforecasters split on four AI benchmarks: MIXED Reality News**
Three hundred thirty-nine AI experts gave four AI benchmark results a 24.6 percent chance, while superforecasters put those same results at 9.7 percent, MIXED Reality News reports. Source: [mixed-news.com](https://mixed-news.com/en/forecasting-research-institute-leap-ai-expert-accuracy/)

### The Board
Will the U.S. invade Iran before 2027? Yes is priced at 16.5 cents, a 16.5 percent implied probability, up 3.0 points in 24 hours, on Polymarket, with 24-hour volume of $758,000, read at 2026-09-26 11:20 UTC.
Whether these venues are available, and for which contracts, depends on where you live; the rules differ by country, province and state and are changing. Source: [polymarket.com](https://polymarket.com/event/will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027)

### New and Notable
Polymarket has listed a new contract on whether the Trump administration is held in contempt over a press ban by October 31, posted at 9:13 a.m. on September 26, 2026. The question is a first listing of a dated contempt deadline tied to a press-access fight, with resolution set at October 31. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Polymarket/status/2103774829396783226)

### How It Works: The Favourite-Longshot Bias
In a parimutuel market, the favorite-longshot bias is a return pattern: the expected return on an outcome tends to rise with the share of bets placed on that outcome. A 2010 paper in the American Economic Journal: Microeconomics treats that pattern as something to test, not as a fixed law. It ties the direction and the size of the bias to the ratio of private information to noise in the market. That ratio, the paper says, should show up in observables: how many people are betting, how many outcomes are on offer, how much private information is around, how much participation comes from recreational interest, whether bets can be divided finely, whether noise arrives after the fact, and whether outcomes were already unequal before anyone bet.

A September 2026 paper looks for the same pattern on Polymarket, using 588 million trades by 2.48 million accounts. In the trades as they happened, purchases below 10 cents lost 19.3 cents per dollar. Purchases at or above 90 cents earned 0.83 cents per dollar. Grouping changes the picture. When each contract is weighted equally, longshots lost 6.3 cents per dollar. When related contracts are first grouped by parent event, those longshots gained 4.1 cents per dollar. The two-sided pattern — cheap contracts losing, expensive ones gaining a little — held in crypto and politics and was absent in sports. Accounts with the strongest past habit of buying longshots, the top tenth, made 26.6 percent of the next month's low-price purchases and earned returns similar to everyone else. The top tenth of accounts that had been buying favorites made 15.1 percent of the next month's high-price purchases and earned less than others. The paper's claim is an aggregate favorite-longshot bias on Polymarket whose size depends on how contracts are grouped. A price near zero or near one is not, on this evidence, a clean read of probability; the grouping of the contract, and whether the market is sports, politics, or crypto, changes the return that price has delivered. Those figures describe past trades. They are not a reason to take either side of any contract.

### How It Works: Calibration: What It Means for a Forecast to Be Right
Calibration means the stated probability matches how often the outcome arrives, across many events rather than one. A sixty percent forecast is calibrated, in that class of calls, if the event happens about sixty percent of the time. Sharpness is separate: probability mass near zero or one, rather than near fifty percent. Sharp and calibrated are not the same thing. One surprising result does not make the forecast wrong, because the score is taken over the set, after the events resolve.

Monthly Weather Review in 2013 describes an improvement to ensemble kernel density model output statistics, called EKDMOS. Model output statistics equations are multiple linear regressions relating observations to ensemble-mean predictors. Spread-skill relationships are one-term linear regressions that predict the ensemble mean’s expected accuracy from the ensemble spread. The method applies the equations to each member, fits a probability density by kernel density fitting, and adjusts that density’s spread to the spread predicted by the spread-skill relationship. On North American Ensemble Forecast System two-meter temperature forecasts from October 1, 2007, through March 31, 2010, the improved EKDMOS forecasts were more reliable than an earlier spread adjustment and than rank-sorting bias-corrected members, with a better calibrated spread-error relationship and more day-to-day spread variability.

Weather and Forecasting in 2010 compares bias correction with spatial disaggregation and an analog method on daily precipitation forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Ensemble Prediction System, over a ten-day period, for the Ohio River basin from 2002 through 2006, against Tropical Rainfall Monitoring Mission observations. Neither beat a simple spatial-interpolation benchmark on forecast skill. Both improved reliability, the analog more so. Bias correction improved the bias for all forecast amounts, less so for large amounts, but the downscaled patterns were unrealistic. The analog reduced biases over a wider range of amounts and produced more realistic patterns.

Reading a market, reliability is whether the price’s implied probability matches later frequency, and sharpness is how far that price sits from fifty percent. Those tests show a fix can improve reliability without improving skill against a simple benchmark. A single resolution does not settle calibration, including when a market is thin or the stake is play money.

# Prediction Markets Daily
> **New York state files lawsuit against Polymarket alleging illegal gambling operation.**

**What You Need to Know:** New York Attorney General Letitia James filed suit against Polymarket on September 24, 2026, claiming the platform runs an illegal gambling operation. Canadian investor group FAIR Canada urged regulators to keep existing limits on prediction market contracts. Metaculus released a new tool tracking community views on AI risks.

### Top Story
New York Attorney General Letitia James and Governor Kathy Hochul filed a lawsuit against Polymarket on September 24, 2026. The complaint alleges the platform operates an illegal gambling business within the state. The action is a filing, not a final ruling. Polymarket faces potential enforcement if the court accepts the claims. Separate reports from CoinGape and WSJ confirm the filing escalates an ongoing state crackdown on prediction markets. The suit names Polymarket directly and seeks to halt operations in New York. Source: [seekingalpha.com](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4646077-polymarket-named-in-lawsuit-filed-by-new-york-state)

### The Ecosystem
Investor advocacy group says existing prediction market restrictions should remain: FAIR Canada: FAIR Canada CEO Jean-Paul Bureaud stated that prediction market contracts remain wagers in substance even if structured as derivatives. The group called for keeping current limits unless broader access proves benefits to investors and the public interest. The statement covers contracts limited to economic, financial or climate matters in Canada. FAIR Canada noted disagreement among regulators, financial firms and academics on whether sports and entertainment contracts fall under securities or gaming rules. The Canadian Securities Administrators ruled last month that sports and entertainment contracts should stay outside securities legislation. Source: [ca.finance.yahoo.com](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/investor-advocacy-group-says-existing-154537705.html)

Chris Christie calls on state attorneys general to target prediction market gambling: CDC Gaming: Former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie urged attorneys general across states to pursue enforcement against prediction market platforms. The call comes amid multiple state actions filed in recent weeks. Source: [cdcgaming.com](https://cdcgaming.com/brief/chris-christie-calls-on-state-attorneys-general-to-target-prediction-market-gambling/)

U.S. gaming lawmakers urge Supreme Court to hear Kalshi case: CDC Gaming: Lawmakers asked the Supreme Court to review the Kalshi litigation over event contracts. The request targets ongoing questions about federal preemption of state gaming laws. Source: [cdcgaming.com](https://cdcgaming.com/brief/u-s-gaming-lawmakers-urge-supreme-court-to-hear-kalshi-case/)

Opinion | Ban prediction markets? That didn’t go well in 1591.: The Washington Post: The column examined historical precedent from 1591 on attempts to restrict similar markets. It argued that earlier bans produced enforcement problems without eliminating trading activity. Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/09/24/prediction-markets-should-not-be-treated-like-casinos/)

### The Board
In early 2028 will an AI generate a full high-quality movie from a prompt priced at 34.9 percent yes on Manifold with 41,000 mana in 24-hour volume read at 2026-09-24 15:52 UTC. Superhuman mathematical problem solving before 2030 assuming no AGI yet priced at 86.5 percent yes on Manifold with 16,000 mana in 24-hour volume read at 2026-09-24 15:52 UTC. 9 percent chance U.S. inflation hits 5 percent in 2026 on Polymarket read at 2026-09-24 15:32. Average weekly earnings in Canada rise 3.2 percent year over year to 1,347.14 dollars on Kalshi read at 2026-09-24 15:51. 2028 Democratic presidential nominee priced at 17 percent for Jon Ossoff on Kalshi with 1.4 million contracts in 24-hour volume read at 2026-09-24 15:52 UTC. Access to these venues depends on where the listener lives. Source: [manifold.markets](https://manifold.markets/ScottAlexander/in-2028-will-an-ai-be-able-to-gener) Source: [manifold.markets](https://manifold.markets/dreev/superhuman-mathematical-problem-sol) Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Polymarket/status/2103145644991152538) Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Kalshi/status/2103150422726721985) Source: [kalshi.com](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxpresnomd)

### New and Notable
Metaculus launched the AI Existential Risk Explorer tool created by Director of Forecasting Ryan Beck. The site displays how forecasters assess AI-caused catastrophe and extinction risks. Dedicated x-risk forecasters on the platform currently price extinction risk at 22 percent while professional forecasters price it at 7.5 percent. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/metaculus/status/2102780872055574713)

### How It Works: Liquidity, Spreads and Thin Markets
Automated market makers in prediction markets recruit third-party liquidity providers who deposit assets and earn fees from trades. The arXiv paper Bootstrapping Liquidity in BTC-Denominated Prediction Markets shows cross-market making against stablecoin venues supplies the most user-friendly risk profile yet requires active professional makers or platform subsidies. The same paper finds DeFi redirection of user trades enables rapid bootstrapping but exposes participants to liquidation thresholds and exchange-rate volatility. A General Theory of Liquidity Provisioning for Prediction Markets demonstrates that protocols allowing arbitrary cost functions can run multiple market makers in parallel while recovering existing DeFi approaches as special cases. Liquidity expressed as a matrix-valued function becomes necessary once three or more securities trade because single-dimensional parameters cannot cover the full price space. Thin markets move sharply on single trades because limited depth leaves wide bid-ask spreads that one order can cross. Listeners can identify thin markets by low 24-hour volume relative to open interest and by observing large price jumps after modest trading activity. The papers note that automated market making remains simple to deploy but carries capital inefficiency and permanent loss risk for providers. Cross-market making trades stability for the need for ongoing professional oversight.

# Prediction Markets Daily
> **CFTC staff say mention markets may be presumed open to manipulation.**

**What You Need to Know:** Staff at the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission told designated contract markets on September 22 that contracts settling on what a named person says, attends or does may be presumed readily susceptible to manipulation. The advisory does not ban those contracts and does not create new legal obligations; it asks exchanges for a heightened showing before listing them. Kalshi is seeking approval for margin on event contracts, Missouri’s attorney general has sent cease-and-desist letters to six operators, and Yahoo Finance has ended a Polymarket deal.

### What This Show Covers
A prediction market lets people trade on whether something will happen. A contract is written around a question and a resolution rule, and the price traders will pay can be read as the crowd’s probability that the answer is yes. That reading is the idea under examination here: when a price works as a forecast, and when the design of the market, the rules, or the people who can move the outcome make it a poor one.

Each episode has the same shape. The regulators, courts and lawmakers deciding what these markets may be come first — the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, state attorneys general and gaming authorities, and regulators outside the United States — and a legal story names the jurisdiction it is actually about. Then the venues, the products and the people building or contesting them. A short board lists a handful of the day’s most traded questions, each with its venue, its volume and the time the price was read, so a probability is never a free-floating number. One explainer walks through how a piece of the machinery works.

This show will not tell anyone what to trade. It reports and explains. It does not recommend buying, selling or holding a contract, and it does not offer a pick, a tip or a view on which side is mispriced. The law is not one rule. It differs by country, province and state, and it is changing; when a story is about the law, the show says whose rules, and it states a specific legal fact only when a dated source supports it.

Prediction Markets Daily is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com. Listeners who want the rest of the network can find it there.

### Top Story
Staff in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Market Oversight issued an advisory on September 22, 2026, covering contracts that settle on specific words or phrases, event attendance, public appearances and interactions between individuals. The guidance, aimed at designated contract markets, says these mention markets can be presumed readily susceptible to manipulation because settlement can depend on conduct controlled by one named person or a small group, unlike contracts on election results, economic releases or regulated sports. It does not ban the contracts and, unlike a Commission rule, creates no new legal obligations; exchanges remain under the Commodity Exchange Act’s Core Principle 3, which requires them to list only derivatives that are not readily susceptible to manipulation, and staff want a heightened showing, with surveillance built around the people who control the outcome. On August 28 the agency ordered former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez to pay $172,539.02 — $107,539.02 in disgorgement and a $65,000 civil penalty — and imposed a three-year trading ban, after finding he used advance access to presidential speeches to trade mention contracts on Kalshi between December 2025 and February 2026. A month before that order, the agency settled with former Representative George Santos over trading in a Kalshi contract on whether he would attend the State of the Union; he paid $35,000 and did not admit wrongdoing. Kalshi said its internal surveillance flagged the Perez trades and that it reported them to federal authorities. Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/financemagnates:c3e1c48a7094b:0-cftc-staff-flag-bets-on-what-people-say-as-presumptively-open-to-manipulation/)

### The Ecosystem

### New and Notable
Polymarket posted a new market, Nothing Ever Happens: September, on the morning of September 23, 2026. The listing puts a month, rather than one candidate or one match, into a single question. Source: [polymarket.com](https://polymarket.com/event/nothing-ever-happens-september-27)

### How It Works: Why a Price Can Be Read as a Probability
A contract that pays a fixed sum if an event happens, and nothing if it does not, trades at a price between those two payoffs. Buyers are taking the view that the event is more likely than that price; sellers, that it is less likely. Where both sides can trade, the price is where that disagreement has cleared for the moment, which is why it can be read as a probability — the terms on which the market last found a counterparty, not a verdict issued by the venue.

A paper in Management Science compared that reading with another way of pooling forecasts. More than 2,400 participants forecast 261 events over two seasons of a geopolitical tournament. They were randomly assigned to prediction markets — continuous double auctions, ranked on earnings — or to prediction polls, submitting probabilities alone or in teams and ranked on Brier scores. In both seasons, market prices were more accurate than the simple mean of the poll forecasts. Team polls outperformed the markets once forecasts were aggregated using temporal decay, weights based on past performance, and recalibration. The polls’ biggest advantage was at the beginning of long-duration questions.

A paper on cost-function market makers notes that trading in a duality-based design collectively implements Follow-The-Regularized-Leader. Modifying that pricing rule, the authors propose a Smooth Quadratic Prediction Market so that trading implements general steepest gradient descent, with a better worst-case monetary loss for AD securities and with no-arbitrage and an instantaneous price preserved. They also look at bounded budgets and buy-only securities, cases where a clean probability reading leaves something out.

The same research flags a limit: independent judgments, properly aggregated, beat market prices at the start of long questions. This show will not say which contract to buy or sell. Every probability here carries its venue, its volume and the time it was read.
